bull.b: The installed-base model generates repeat instrument, accessory and service purchases linked to procedures. This recurring mix improves revenue visibility and creates durable monetization as system utilization and placements expand.

High gross and operating margins, strong cash conversion and substantial free cash flow provide resources for R&D, commercial investment and shareholder returns. The near-zero-debt balance sheet further supports resilience through industry or policy volatility.

A growing installed base strengthens Intuitive’s clinical ecosystem, service relationships and recurring instrument demand. Continued adoption across specialties, including SP and ION, expands the company’s long-term procedure opportunity and switching advantages.

bear.b: Slower growth raises the importance of sustained procedure expansion, new indications and international execution. If the installed base matures or utilization growth moderates, operating leverage and expectations for future earnings expansion could weaken.

China’s tender-driven market and increasing local competition can limit system placements, pricing and future recurring procedures. Continued policy and funding uncertainty in other international markets also creates a structural constraint on geographic diversification.

The razor-and-blades model depends on instrument consumption and pricing. Extended-use products and a shift toward lower-value procedure categories could reduce revenue per case, pressuring recurring growth and margins even if procedure volumes continue rising.
